Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week. HelioHealth's security and clinical teams liked the private deployment model, but procurement asked for a clearer breakdown of where the platform fee vs licensing sits, and what support bands would look like for a multi-site rollout (3 US sites + one DR site).

Two specific asks from procurement:
- Can platform fee be banded by commit tiers (pilot vs production) rather than flat annual?
- Is there room for a 12-month discounted starter fee tied to an implementation SOW acceptance (we'd sign the SOW quickly if we can get a short-term concession)?

Would appreciate a short note and a proposed sketch we can take to our CFO.

Best,

Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment commercial ask

Hi Jared —

Thanks for the clear asks. Quick high-level response below; attaching a concise pricing summary for the VPC/on-prem packaging. Marissa (commercial lead) and Karthik (solutions / onprem ops) are looped in to confirm feasibility.

Proposal sketch:
- Platform fee: tiered banding by committed annual consumption (Pilot: $35k/mo band; Production small: $75k/mo band; Production large: $160k/mo band). Bands include the private control plane, telemetry retention baseline, and minor feature backports.
- Licensing (on-prem runtime): one-time operator license per site + per-GPU node unit pricing (invoiceable at signing of SOW).
- Support tiers: Standard (business hours, 24x5, response SLA 4 hrs) included in platform band. Premium (24x7 oncall, 2-hr response, incident bridge) available as add-on retainer.
- Implementation concession: we can offer a timebound 12-month reduction of the platform fee by 20% for the pilot band if SOW signed within 30 days and a 6-month runway commit is accepted. This concession is structured as a credit on invoices, not a permanent price change.

Open items: 1) precise node counts to firm up operator license totals; 2) whether Helio wants the DR site licensed active or cold standby (affects licensing).

I'll let Marissa follow up with a short commercial term summary and a redlineable SOW.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Commercial, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_VPC_Pricing_Summary_v3.pdf

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment commercial ask — term summary

Jared —

Following Neha's sketch, proposed commercial bullets (for procurement to review):
1) Pilot band concession: 20% credit to platform fee for first 12 months, triggered by SOW signing within 30 days. Pilot defined as up to 3 nodes, single site.
2) Production banding: specify committed annual throughput bucket (tokens/month) to determine platform band. Transition from pilot->production can be exercised once during first 12 months.
3) Operator + node licensing: invoiced at SOW acceptance; license transfers not permitted without notice; standard decommission credits given if truly unused after 6 months.
4) Support retainer: Premium retainer priced as $12k/mo (24x7) or $6k/mo (extended hours) per account; can be amortized into annual invoice.
5) Exit / migration: if Helio converts to hosted within 24 months, migration credit equals remaining platform credit pro-rata.

If procurement wants, we can convert these bullets into short contract language (3-4 clauses) for their legal team.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Director, Enterprise Commercials
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -07:00

Hi Patrick —

Short answers from ops: 
- Operator entitlements: per-cluster. If you run multiple clusters in a site, each cluster needs an operator entitlement; we can issue a pooled license for contiguous clusters under a single account to simplify accounting, but the technical entitlement remains per-cluster.
- Pilot concession visibility: yes, the 20% credit will be explicitly shown on the SOW and a corresponding invoice credit schedule will be attached.
- SLA measurement: SLAs are measured from Redwood incident creation timestamp. To avoid confusion we recommend a joint runbook step where Helio triggers a Redwood incident via our portal — that timestamp will be the SLA start. We can add a clause in the SOW to formalize the handoff.

I'll work with Marissa to add a short table mapping committed throughput -> platform band and include node/license math.

Thanks,
